newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat slips lower in thin pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat slips lower in thin pre-holiday trade.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures slipped lower in thin pre-holiday trade, and traders said the market was taking pressure from weaker world wheat prices.
U.S. wheat markets rallied last week amid concern over possible weather-related damage to U.S. and Argentine crops. But as those fears faded, prices have eased.
"There's absolutely nothing going on," said a trader, looking over at the nearly empty wheat pit.
At 1213 CST, KCBT wheat was two to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 3-3/4 cents at $4.08.
Traders said Shay Grain and Wolcott Lincoln each sold at least 300,000 March bushels.
